data.gender_notes: Ranjay is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Joyful, Delight, Pleasure, Wish Fulfillment, Raja, King, Power, Victory, and Virtuous. The name Ranjay carries the meaning “Joyful, Delight, Pleasure” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Ranjay usually hope their child will grow to embody joyful, delight, pleasure and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ranjay" in Hindu culture holds profound significance as it embodies several noble qualities such as joy, Raja (king), power, and victory. In ancient India, names were often given to newborns based on their horoscopes or observable qualities at birth. The name "Ranjay," when given, suggested a hopeful and prosperous future for the child.

historical_references.reference: Ranjit Singh, also known as Maharaj Ranjit Singh, was a Sikh military and political leader who is best known for establishing and ruling the Sikh Empire in the Punjab region of India during the late 18th and early 19th centuries. He gained control of Lahore in 1799, and by 1801, had consolidated his power over the whole of the Punjab. He was also known as 'Sher-e-Punjab' or 'the lion of Punjab'.

Ranji, a Hindu king of the Maratha confederacy in western India during the late 17th and early 18th centuries, ruled the territories around present-day Maharashtra and Gujarat. He is known for his military campaigns against the Mughal Empire and for establishing the Maratha kingdom as a major power in the region. He was also known as 'Maharaja Ranji' or 'Maharaja Jaisingh' and is considered one of the greatest rulers of the Maratha confederacy.
